## Sophia modules (sophia.html) · 10 passages

- **ep**: Steven Hoffenberg hired him around 1987 to help raise capital for Towers Financial Corporation, at $25,000 a month — roughly $70,000 a month in present terms. Together they attempted a corporate raid on Pan Am using Towers as the vehicle, unsuccessfully. This is the first documented instance of a very large sum moving to him outside any ordinary compensation structure — the same shape as the townhouse transfer three years later.
- **ep**: He founded his own wealth-management firm in 1988 while still consulting for Hoffenberg, reportedly stating a minimum client threshold in the hundreds of millions. The firm was private, had no disclosure obligation, and produced no audited track record. For years its only publicly known billionaire client would be one man, and that relationship began in this window.

Hoffenberg pleaded guilty to five counts and served eighteen years of a twenty-year sentence. Epstein, who had left around 1989, was never charged, and no public record explains the charging decision. The impunity pattern appears here for the first time, fifteen years before the agreement everyone knows about.
